intent: A single operating theatre, then the quiet rival four years earlier, then the news racing across the ocean: the day pain was switched off.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where was the FIRST surgery under anaesthesia?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where was the first surgery under anaesthesia?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The USA. On 16 October 1846 at Massachusetts General in Boston a dentist put a patient to sleep with ether.

lines.direction: tighten on Boston; a HELD DOWN plate waits at the bottom — how surgery used to be; a tooth sticker on 'Morton' becomes a stethoscope on 'Warren'; on 'nothing' the plate wipes away, the NO PAIN card lands with a sleeping-face sticker; the US flag-ball relaxes
lines.text: Morton held the sponge; John Warren cut a tumour from Gilbert Abbott's neck. He felt nothing.

lines.direction: ease south-west so Boston and Georgia share the frame; the Jefferson pin on 'Jefferson'; a year counter ticks 1842 → 1846 on 'earlier'; a shushing-face sticker on 'unpublished'; the Boston pin leaves at the end
lines.text: But Crawford Long of Jefferson, Georgia had done it 4 years earlier, unpublished.

lines.direction: pull right out over the Atlantic; an envelope sticker rides the line from Boston to London until 'London'; the London pin and tag land; a flag-ball for Britain thinks; the US pulses on 'December'
lines.text: Within 2 months London heard, and Robert Liston amputated a leg under ether that December.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
